assertion.rationale: F1: data-api had ingressExternal:true and zero inbound authentication (app.ts:56) — anyone who found the FQDN could read Defender posture, Dependabot alerts and Log Analytics results, and loop full table scans. F1 is now CLOSED (Task 6): infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep's dataApiApp module sets ingressExternal:false, so the app is reachable only from inside the Container Apps environment. Both frontends already proxied /api/ server-side before this change — control-tower's and launch-ops' nginx.conf.template both carry a `location /api/ { proxy_pass ${DATA_API_ORIGIN}/; ... }` rule, verified present in both rather than assumed — so no legitimate caller lost access; DATA_API_ORIGIN still resolves the app's FQDN, which Azure Container Apps assigns to internal-ingress apps too. The /healthz convenience the app's header comment previously cited is now reached with `az containerapp exec` instead of a browser. F2: the MCP auth gate was inert in the shipped configuration — it threw only in backendMode 'cloud', MLS_TOOL_BACKENDS is set nowhere in infra/ or .github/, so /healthz reported auth.enforced:false to anyone. F2 is now CLOSED (Tasks 4 and 5). Task 4 closed the application half: loadInboundAuth (auth-gate.ts) no longer conditions enforcement on backendMode, so local mode — the configuration that actually ships — now fails closed at boot without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN or an explicit MCP_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED opt-out, and the gate is mounted ahead of the body parser. Task 5 closed the infra half: infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep no longer declares a `@secure()` mcpAuthToken parameter (deleted, along with demo.bicepparam's empty default); the mcp-tools container app instead resolves the mcp-auth-token secret directly from the platform Key Vault at runtime via a keyVaultUrl + identity reference, using a Key Vault Secrets User grant on the mcp-tools UAMI (module mcpKvGrant, reusing modules/key-vault-secrets-user-role.bicep, previously unreferenced since the 2026-08-24 Anthropic removal). The token therefore never enters this template, demo.bicepparam, ARM deployment history or a what-if log, and no workflow reads or exports it. MLS_TOOL_BACKENDS is now set explicitly via the mcpToolsBackendMode parameter (default 'local') instead of being absent from every workflow. F3: the Direct Line token endpoint minted tokens to unauthenticated callers whenever DIRECTLINE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS was unset or Origin was absent, and that path carries the MCP token, which made F2's gate irrelevant to it. F3 is now CLOSED (Task 7): directline-token.mjs now refuses with 500 when the allow-list is unset (so an unbound token is never minted) and with 403 when Origin is absent or not allow-listed, checked as two separate conditions rather than one combined boolean so neither can skip the other. F13: zero workload RBAC is expressed anywhere in IaC — the only role assignments in the estate are deployer-to-Owner and verifier-to-Reader, both at subscription scope in PowerShell; seven documented workload grants (data-api, mcp-tools, cost-ingest) exist nowhere as code, so access is not limited to authorized users, processes or devices by construction. Task 12 expresses five of the seven in code: infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep now grants data-api and mcp-tools Log Analytics Reader (scoped to the platform LAW, modules/log-analytics-reader-role.bicep) and Security Reader (subscription scope, modules/workload-role-assignments.bicep), mcp-tools additionally gets Cost Management Reader (same module), data-api's SQL contained-database user is expressed in data/seed/sql/900-contained-users.sql, and data-api's Fabric workspace Viewer grant is expressed via a new Add-FabricWorkspaceRoleAssignment function in infra/fabric/fabric-api.psm1, reached through provision-workspace.ps1's -DataApiPrincipalId parameter. CORRECTION (F24, final branch review): an earlier revision of this sentence said that parameter was 'wired'. It was not - nothing passed it, and layer-05-fabric.yml structurally could not, because L5 runs before L7 creates the identity. The capability existed; the invocation did not. F24 added the post-L7 step in layer-07-apps.yml that actually passes it, mirroring the F20 step Task 22 added for the SQL grant. So five of F13's seven grants landed in Task 12/17, the sixth landed with F24, and the seventh remains blocked on F19. Task 17 (F15, now CLOSED) lands the sixth: `az costmanagement export create`/`update` has no `--identity-type` flag, and the costmanagement CLI extension pins API version 2020-06-01, which hard-requires the destination storage account's shared keys to be enabled (github.com/Azure/azure-cli/issues/32912) — it 400s outright against this account's `allowSharedKeyAccess: false`. layer-06-platform.yml therefore creates the export via `az rest` against the Exports REST API directly (api-version 2023-08-01), requesting `identity: { type: SystemAssigned }` in the PUT body, and grants that identity's `principalId` (read back from the same PUT response, never a resourceId or clientId) Storage Blob Data Contributor via an explicit `az role assignment create`, scoped to the `cost-exports` container. One of the seven remains unexpressed and F13 stays OPEN because of it: cost-ingest -> Storage Blob Data Reader is blocked on F19 (cost-ingest has no Function App, and therefore no identity, anywhere in this repo's IaC, despite infra-up.yml:31 claiming otherwise). Building Task 12 also surfaced F20 (the SQL grant above is expressed but nothing re-ran the seed script after L7 creates the identity, so it did not yet apply in a single infra-up.yml pass — CLOSED by Task 22, which added a -SchemaOnly mode to data/seed/seed.ps1 / sql-seed.psm1's Invoke-SqlSeed, applying data/seed/sql/*.sql without requiring data/generated/ or a row-count check, invoked from layer-07-apps.yml's deploy job right after the apps deployment so the identity already exists) and F21 (mls-verifier's own documented Fabric workspace Viewer grant did not exist either, breaking the L5 Verifier audit — a different principal, tracked separately; CLOSED by Task 21, which wires provision-workspace.ps1's -VerifierPrincipalId — reusing the same Add-FabricWorkspaceRoleAssignment path this control's F13 grant above already uses — through layer-05-fabric.yml's deploy job, which resolves mls-verifier's service-principal object ID via `az ad sp show`). F20 and F21 were never contributors to this control (its evidence array above cites F1/F2/F3/F13 only; F20 maps to no 800-171 control per compliance/findings/2026-08-26-prepublication-review.md#f20, F21 likewise per .../#f21) — noted here only because this rationale referenced them in passing, and that reference must stay accurate. Overall status stays GAP: F1, F2 and F3 are all now closed, but F13 remains open — six of seven grants landed, one did not (F19) — and is this control's only remaining contributor. CORRECTION (2026-08-28, final pre-publication audit -- F25). The sentence above about Task 6 closing F1 was written from F1's own Fix text and was INCOMPLETE, and the clause it leaned on -- "both frontends already proxy /api/ server-side" -- was the bypass rather than the reason internal ingress sufficed. control-tower and launch-ops were themselves ingressExternal:true with NO authConfig, and both nginx.conf.template files blind-proxy `location /api/ { proxy_pass ${DATA_API_ORIGIN}/; }` with no credential and no path allowlist, so GET https://<control-tower-fqdn>/api/feeds/secure-score reached data-api unauthenticated from the public internet -- against an identity holding Security Reader at SUBSCRIPTION scope. F25 closes it: infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep now puts Container Apps Easy Auth (entraEasyAuthConfig(), RedirectToLoginPage, an Entra provider with only a public clientId and openIdIssuer, tokenStore disabled, no client secret) in front of launch-ops, control-tower AND compliance, and each app's ingressExternal is the same expression as "is Easy Auth configured", so no parameter combination publishes one of them without authentication. excludedPaths is ['/healthz'] and nothing else, so nothing under /api/ is reachable without a session. .github/workflows/layer-07-apps.yml resolves MLS_LAUNCH_OPS_CLIENT_ID, MLS_CONTROL_TOWER_CLIENT_ID and MLS_COMPLIANCE_CLIENT_ID from the Entra app registrations L3 creates, treating a hand-set variable as an override; an ID it cannot resolve leaves that app internal-only rather than failing the deploy or publishing it open (F36 -- an earlier revision of this workflow refused to deploy at all without all three, which made the F25 fix undeployable out of the box, and is the claim this sentence used to carry). F26, found alongside it: the runbook's claim that an unset MLS_COMPLIANCE_CLIENT_ID made ARM reject the deployment was false -- an undefined GitHub variable expands to the EMPTY STRING, so readEnvironmentVariable returned '' and never reached its 'unset' default (reproduced against Bicep CLI 0.46.1); the guard now treats empty and 'unset' alike. Verified by verification/tests/frontend-auth.Tests.ps1 (14 assertions, each mutation-tested) and az bicep build; nothing has been deployed. CLOSED (2026-08-28, commit c33f06e -- F19, on explicit sponsor authorisation). F13's seventh and last documented grant -- cost-ingest -> Storage Blob Data Reader -- is now expressed in code. It could not be before: F19 meant apps/cost-ingest, a complete and tested Azure Functions app, appeared in no Bicep anywhere, so it had no Function App, no identity, and therefore no principal for the grant to be written against. infra/bicep/platform/main.bicep now provisions the Function App on a Flex Consumption (FC1) plan with a user-assigned identity, and grants that identity Storage Blob Data Reader (2a2b9908-6ea1-4ae2-8e65-a410df84e7d1) scoped to the cost-exports CONTAINER -- not the storage account and not the subscription -- via the new infra/bicep/platform/modules/blob-container-role.bicep. Flex Consumption is a least-privilege choice as much as a cost one: it is the only plan that supports a managed-identity AzureWebJobsStorage with no Azure Files shared-key connection string, so the Function introduces no stored credential (CLAUDE.md hard rule 5); and because that plan supports only the Event Grid-based blob trigger, the Function keeps no blob receipts or poison queue in the account it watches, which is what lets the grant there stay a pure read. The three account-wide roles the Functions host requires (Storage Blob Data Owner, Storage Queue Data Contributor, Storage Table Data Contributor) bind to a SECOND, empty runtime storage account created for that purpose, never to the cost-export account -- consolidating them would have handed the identity Owner-class blob access to the very container this grant narrows it to. Its OneLake write access is Fabric workspace Contributor (infra/fabric/provision-workspace.ps1, -CostIngestPrincipalId, wired from layer-07-apps.yml): Viewer is read-only and cannot create Files/cost_daily/, Contributor is the lowest of Fabric's four workspace roles that can write, and Fabric exposes no data-plane role narrower than the workspace -- it is the broadest grant any workload identity holds in this estate and is argued for at the grant itself. STATUS MOVES TO CLOSED because every finding this review raised against this control is now addressed -- F1, F2 and F3 (Tasks 6, 4/5 and 7), F25 and F26 (the final pre-publication audit), F24 (the final branch review), and now F13 -- and CLOSED here means exactly what compliance/README.md's Register vocabulary says it means: no known open finding stands against this control. It is not a claim that the control is met, that the estate was assessed exhaustively, or that anything was verified against a live tenant. WHAT IS AND IS NOT VERIFIED. Nothing in this estate has ever been deployed; no Azure, Entra or Fabric call was made to build or test any of this. The evidence is repo-static -- it describes what the repository DECLARES. verification/tests/cost-ingest.Tests.ps1 (43 assertions) asserts the role definition GUID and the container scope against comment-stripped Bicep, never against comment text (the F27 ruling), refuses any role GUID outside the four this leg documents, and checks that the account-wide host roles bind only to the runtime storage account; infra/fabric/tests/provision-workspace.Tests.ps1 asserts the Fabric role string per principal. Three surgical mutations were run against those suites and each turned exactly the intended assertions red: widening the container grant to account scope (1 failure), dropping the user-assigned identity (1 failure), widening the Fabric role to Member (6 failures). STILL OUTSTANDING, and carried in the recommendation below rather than dropped: F13's Fix text also called for a V7.x audit criterion asserting each principal holds exactly its expected roles and no others. That does not exist. A live-tenant criterion has never had a tenant to assert against, and the static tests above guard what this repository declares, not what any subscription holds.

recommendation: No open finding remains against this control. All seven of F13's documented workload RBAC grants are expressed in IaC, data-api is internal-ingress behind Easy Auth along with both frontends and the compliance board, the MCP auth gate fails closed by default with its token resolved from Key Vault, and the Direct Line token endpoint fails closed on an unset or unmatched origin (Tasks 4, 5, 6, 7, 12, 17, F24, F25, F26 and F19). STILL OUTSTANDING: add a V7.x Verifier criterion asserting that each workload principal holds exactly its expected roles at exactly its expected scopes, and no others, read back from ARM as mls-verifier. All seven grants are now expressed in IaC and guarded by static tests over this repository, but no criterion has ever compared that declaration against a deployed tenant -- because nothing has ever been deployed.
